report:
## Conclusion

**No. High-quality evidence indicates that saw palmetto (*Serenoa repens*) preparations do not meaningfully improve benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) symptoms over the longer term compared with placebo.**

The strongest evidence is a 2023 Cochrane review of 27 randomized trials involving 4,656 men. It concluded that saw palmetto alone provides **little to no benefit** for lower urinary tract symptoms caused by prostatic enlargement. At longer-term follow-up of **12 to 17 months**, it produced no significant improvement in urinary symptoms or quality of life versus placebo.  
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37345871/  
https://www.aafp.org/afp/2024/0500/cochrane-saw-palmetto-benign-prostatic-hyperplasia

This conclusion is supported by two rigorous longer trials:

- A one-year double-blind trial of 225 men with moderate-to-severe BPH found saw palmetto was **not superior to placebo** for symptoms, urinary flow, prostate size, or other objective measures.  
  https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa053085

- The 72-week CAMUS trial of 369 men tested escalating doses up to three times the usual amount and likewise found **no benefit over placebo at any dose**.  
  https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/1104439

Saw palmetto appears generally well tolerated, with adverse-event rates similar to placebo, but product composition can vary. Overall, men with persistent or worsening urinary symptoms should seek medical assessment rather than rely on saw palmetto as an effective long-term BPH treatment.
